title: R' Yitzchak bar Maryon
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In the Jerusalem Talmud, Sukkah ch. 2, halakhah 5, he asked R' Elazar; and in Yalkut Tehillim, remez 859, he said in the name of R-L (ר״ל), 'Kindness is from eternity' (and Hyman says this saying is drawn from the Jerusalem Talmud, Peah ch. 1, halakhah 1, folio 2b; there R' Yochanan son of R' Maryon [speaks] in the name of R' Yochanan); and in Yevamot, end of ch. 6, he said in the name of R' Chanina. And in Tanchuma, Re'eh 16, R' Azariah and R' Yonatan ben Chagai and R' Yitzhak bar Maryon [speak] in the name of R' Yosi son of R' Chanina; and in Bereshit Rabbah 74:10 [supplied פ״ער־י], Rabbi Azariah in the name of Rabbi Chagai and Rabbi Yitzhak bar Maryon; and Hyman says it should likewise read this way in Midrash Tehillim 31:6 (where he says 'ben Tardion' is an error), as it is stated there at 78:19.

And he is mentioned in Shabbat ch. 2, halakhah 6, as having said: Were it not written, 'He who makes a way in the sea,' a person would die as soon as he entered it; and the saying is quoted in Midrash Tehillim 104:23.
And likewise he is mentioned in Bereshit Rabbah ch. 6, [section] 5, and in Kohelet Rabbah 3:11: Rabbi Ivo and Rabbi Huna, in his name [supplied בשמי, “in my name”].

notes.text: The Bereshit Rabbah chapter label פ״ער־י is irregular; the final speaker’s initials ר״ה remain unexpanded.

The heading and p001 remain R'; no title from a matching later citation is transferred to the heading or separate passages. All unsupported personal titles in the Sukkah, Yalkut, Peah, Yevamot and Tanchuma portions remain abbreviated. The father-title components in Peah's בר׳ מריון and Tanchuma's בר׳ חנינא are separately preserved as son of R' Maryon and son of R' Chanina; Chagai in the earlier patronymic is untitled. R-L (ר״ל) remains literal; the older Resh Lakish expansion is an inherited contextual identification, not newly bound here. Kindness is from eternity retains the source's מעולם without importing a new proof verse or an era. The claim that the saying comes from Peah is Hyman's, and the Yochanan and Yitzhak reporters remain distinct. Peah's supplied chapter1/halakhah1 and following ב: remain rendered folio2b by convention, not a range1–2 or newly verified numbering. Four whole saved primary scalars were read, with raw SHA256, selectors and actual edition metadata checked: TE Bereshit Rabbah6:5, TE74:10, TE Kohelet Rabbah3:11:2, and OYW Midrash Tehillim31 selected text[3]. TE74:10 explicitly has Rabbi Azariah in the name of Rabbi Chagai and Rabbi Yitzchak bar Maron, supporting full titles only for that local chain. The supplied פ״ער־י remains unresolved beside the digital74:10 comparison, and Hyman's Maryon מריון is retained beside the digital מרון; there is no letter-repair or correction-history claim. The earlier70:10 nonmatch remains a bounded historical observation, not absence from all witnesses. Hyman's וכן צ״ל retains its definite should-read force; his declaration that ben Tardion is erroneous stays attributed, not adopted into Hebrew or an identity binding. OYW has full Rabbi Yitzchak ben Tardion in the selected scalar, but that title does not transfer to Hyman's proposed different name. Hyman's31:6 and78:19 stay supplied locators, not a new edition mapping. TE6:5 contains the sea phrase and Rabbi Yitzchak bar Maryon locally; it does not independently verify the separate Shabbat2hal6 or Midrash Tehillim104:23 citation, nor does its title move to the heading. The counterfactual were-it-not-written and immediate-death consequence stay intact. TE Kohelet3:11:2 explicitly has Rabbi Bivai, Rabbi Ivo and Rabbi Huna reporting Rabbi Yitzchak bar Maryon: the two names supplied by Hyman support Rabbi Ivo/Rabbi Huna here only. Bivai, omitted by Hyman, is not imported. Hyman's בשמי remains in my name in the translation, while the digital בשם רבי יצחק בר מריון is recorded separately; the proposed replacement by in his name is not applied. The old Hoshaya guess and current unexpanded-initials note remain archived exactly, with this additive qualification. The Sukkah Elazar/Laazar spelling comparison is inherited, not a newly selected whole Yerushalmi scalar this pass. No longer primary discourse, additional speakers, scriptural continuation, sword statement or historical identity is imported. Every old English version and all three original mixed notes plus the current note remain exact. Both p002 and p004 source holds remain.

The consulted scan of Hyman II, p. 796, prints Bereshit Rabbah פ״עד־י, 74:10, and ends with Rabbi Ivo and R-H בשמו, “in his name.” These differ from the supplied פ״ער־י and בשמי, “in my name.” The English follows those printed readings, while the supplied Hebrew and all earlier notes remain unchanged. The whole consulted Kohelet Rabbah 3:11:2 names Bivai, Ivo and Huna reporting Yitzhak bar Maryon; Hyman’s omitted Bivai is not inserted. Bereshit Rabbah 74:10 has Azariah in Chagai’s name and Yitzhak bar Maron, beside Hyman’s Maryon. The whole consulted Peah 1:1 passage names Yochanan bar Maria in Yochanan’s name, not Yitzhak; this comparison does not merge the reporters or establish Hyman’s precise old folio numbering. The whole Shabbat 2:6 passage confirms the counterfactual sea saying and its immediate-death consequence. The parallel in the consulted Midrash Tehillim 104, paragraph 17, names Morion, beside Hyman’s 104:23 locator. Midrash Tehillim 31, paragraph 4, names Yitzhak ben Tardion, while chapter 78, paragraph 16, gives the corresponding sixteen-sided-sword saying under Yitzhak bar Maryon. These modern locations differ from Hyman’s 31:6 and 78:19; his definite instruction to correct Tardion remains his proposal, not an admitted identity or a silent alteration of the Midrash. His other transmission and chronological claims, the literal R-L and the exact uncollated editions remain attributed. Additional speakers, legal discussion, scriptural proofs and the sword saying itself are not imported into this abbreviated biography.
